title: apt is broken: the kernel update failed halfway
intro: Patching web-07 fails: every apt command now ends with 'E: Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg returned an error code (1)'. The host is still running, but it can't install anything, including security fixes, and it may not boot cleanly into a kernel.

steps.prompt: Try to let dpkg finish its interrupted work, and read the error.
steps.fake_output:
Setting up linux-image-5.15.0-122-generic (5.15.0-122.132) ...
update-initramfs: Generating /boot/initrd.img-5.15.0-122-generic
gzip: stdout: No space left on device
E: mkinitramfs failure gzip 1
dpkg: error processing package linux-image-5.15.0-122-generic (--configure)

steps.prompt: No space left while writing the initramfs to /boot. Check /boot.
steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda2       488M  488M     0 100% /boot

steps.prompt: Find out which kernel is running (you must not remove that one).
List the kernel images present in /boot.
steps.fake_output:
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-97-generic
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-101-generic
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-105-generic
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-112-generic
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-119-generic
-rw------- 1 root root 11M /boot/vmlinuz-5.15.0-122-generic

steps.prompt: apt can't run autoremove while dpkg is broken. Purge the oldest kernel, 5.15.0-97 (packages linux-image-5.15.0-97-generic and linux-modules-5.15.0-97-generic), directly with dpkg to free space.
steps.fake_output:
Removing linux-image-5.15.0-97-generic (5.15.0-97.107) ...
Purging configuration files for linux-image-5.15.0-97-generic ...
(/boot: 41M freed)
steps.hint: dpkg --purge works even when apt's dependency state is broken.

steps.prompt: Now let apt finish the kernel installation and remove the rest of the old kernels.
expected_commands: sudo apt -f install && sudo apt autoremove --purge -y
sudo apt --fix-broken install && sudo apt autoremove --purge -y
steps.fake_output:
Setting up linux-image-5.15.0-122-generic (5.15.0-122.132) ...
update-initramfs: Generating /boot/initrd.img-5.15.0-122-generic
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  linux-image-5.15.0-101-generic* linux-image-5.15.0-105-generic* linux-image-5.15.0-112-generic*
(/boot: 43% used)
steps.hint: apt -f install fixes broken installs; then autoremove.

resolution: /boot was a small 488MB partition, and six kernels had accumulated because nothing ever removed old ones. The kernel update filled it while building the new initramfs, leaving dpkg half-configured, and apt refuses to do anything while dpkg is broken. The catch-22 is that the normal cleanup (apt autoremove) is exactly what's blocked, so you free space with dpkg directly (never the running kernel), let 'apt -f install' finish, and then clean up properly. Why it matters: a half-installed kernel with a missing initramfs can leave the host unbootable at its next reboot. Prevention: autoremove as part of every patch run (and 'installonly_limit' on RHEL), monitoring /boot like any other filesystem, and larger /boot partitions (1GB) in new images.
